newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: YACHTING-Yatching's 'Auld Mug' to be restored after attack.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-Yatching's 'Auld Mug' to be restored after attack.

text.p: One of sport's oldest and most prestigious trophies, yatching's America's Cup, would be restored after being damaged in a sledge hammer attack last week, cup holders, Team New Zealand, said on Tuesday.

A Maori political activist, Benjamin Peri Nathan, was charged on Saturday with criminal damage and trespass after using a sledge hammer to smash the toughened glass case and badly dent the mid section and neck of the jug-shaped cup.
British jewellers Garrards, which made the cup, have said they can and will completely restore the trophy in six weeks, Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron Commodore John Heise said.
"The cup itself has been released by the police and it now remains for Sun Alliance, our insurers, to complete their assessment of the damage," Heise said.
Sun donated NZ$500,000 (US$350,000) of insurance on the cup.
The 150 year-old cup was on display at the Royal New Zealand Yatch Club under electronic security when the attack took place. Security arrangements were being reviewed, Heise said.
Nathan was remanded in custody for a hearing on April 18 and his lawyer indicated he will deny the charges and elect trial by jury.
The attack on the cup caused outrage here and in the United States, where it has spent most its life.
